what: FINAL COMMITTED RECOMMENDATION (agent-verified, 2026-04-21): Option B — Minified JS on npm. NOT Bun compile, NOT yao-pkg, NOT Rust. Rationale: user's two stated goals are (1) minimize changes/risk to current aide-memory, (2) minimize ability for people to get source code. Minified-npm satisfies both at ~1 day cost vs 2-3 weeks + ongoing ops burden for binary approaches. All binary options produce the same mangled/bundled JS when extracted via `unbuned`/`bun-decompile` in 1-3 minutes — they don't provide meaningfully better protection for these goals than minified npm with source maps excluded. Bun's `--bytecode` flag is explicitly NOT protection per Bun's own docs. Implementation: `esbuild src/cli/aide-memory.ts --bundle --platform=node --target=node18 --minify --external:better-sqlite3 --external:*.node`, `package.aide-memory.json` files allowlist, CI `scripts/verify-tarball.js` that fails if any .ts/.map/src/ in tarball, bump to 0.1.2. Keep `tsc` for dev/tests unchanged. No shim, no binary, no signing, no AV handling, no cross-platform matrix. **BRANCH STRATEGY: abandon feature/binary entirely. The --scan removal I did in Phase 0 is REDUNDANT — feature/phase-1 already absorbed it in commit 6be74e6 ("Phase 1 validation fixes — M, I, Settings, --scan removal"). feature/phase-1@71f8a9b has scan.ts deleted, --scan removed from CLI, plus further work (mid-session drift-repair, E2E validation guide). Start a new branch `feature/minified-npm` off CURRENT feature/phase-1 HEAD (71f8a9b), not off feature/binary.** Keep `pre-binary-migration` tag (zero cost) as historical rollback marker but discard feature/binary commits. OSCILLATION HISTORY in this session went Bun→yao-pkg→Bun→hybrid→Bun→back-to-minified-npm across ~10 turns; final answer reached after agent-verified primary-source check confirmed Bun --bytecode isn't protection + confirmed extraction tools work in seconds. Future reviewers: apply extra scrutiny per memory 149/153, but final recommendation anchored in primary Bun docs.
